It solves the problem of local minima inherent to sparse, locally supported representations in generalizable novel view synthesis, where non-differentiable pruning or splitting cannot be applied because gradients must back-propagate through the representation [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the core problem statement and solution described in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that optimizing primitive parameters directly suffers from local minima, and while single-scene optimization uses non-differentiable pruning/splitting, the generalizable case requires back-propagating gradients through the representation, making non-differentiable operations inapplicable. The source confirms that pixelSplat solves this by predicting a dense probability distribution and using a differentiable sampling operation (reparameterization trick) to allow gradient flow, thereby avoiding the local minima inherent to sparse, locally supported representations.
